newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Former Sri Lankan minister held in police custody.
newsitem.headline: Former Sri Lankan minister held in police custody.

text.p: A former minister has been detained under Sri Lanka's sweeping emergency regulations, his lawyers said on Tuesday.
Sirisena Cooray, a minister in the former United National Party government, was arrested late on Monday, they said.
"He is being held under detention orders issued by the Defence Secretary," lawyer Sarath Kongahage told Reuters.

Cooray, who can be detained for up to three months without being charged, was detained to prevent him from acting in any manner prejudicial to national security or public order, Kongahage quoted police as saying.
"We intend to file a fundamental rights case in the Supreme Court on Wednesday," Kongahage added.
He said no charges had been formally brought against Cooray, who was minister of housing and local government and a confidant of assassinated UNP president Ranasinghe Premadasa.
The UNP's 17-year reign ended in 1994 when the ruling People's Alliance, headed by President Chandrika Kumaratunga, won presidential and general elections.

Cooray, who returned to the island in April after a lengthy stay abroad, has been ordered to appear before two presidential commissions probing election malpractices and the death of a senior UNP politician in 1993.
UNP politicians said Cooray was organising a mass rally on June 29 to commemorate Premadasa, a populist leader who was killed by separatist Tamil rebels in 1993, at the time of his arrest.
